Gate change (tools/hooks/pre-commit): candidate set = fast pool ∪ declared scripts; coverage now uses prefix matching; a declared out-of-pool script RUNS when a staged change touches its module (the select fix) while pool narrowing is preserved; the selection runs in bounded parallelism (TEST_GATE_WORKERS=6); on failure, a script in the known-red baseline is reported KNOWN RED non-blocking and any failure NOT in the baseline REFUSES the commit; the dishonest 'change-based selection active' message now reports the real declaration count (and the zero-declaration case says so instead of claiming selection is active).

The baseline is dated 2026-08-24, per-script (one `known-red <script> <owner> <disposition>` line each), owned (T442, T518, T682, T337, T454, T466, T821, D021, or stream2b-green where triage is that sprint's job), and expiring.

== THE BUDGET (tension a), RESOLVED ==
Serial wall of the largest declared pre-commit suite (src/managent, ~25 scripts) is ~90s — over the 45s budget. Two halves close the gap, neither alone is enough: (1) tiered placement — scripts >20s standalone (or needing a build arg, or state-dependent) are not selected at commit time, they run in `zig build test`; (2) bounded parallelism — 6 workers, wall dominated by the single slowest selected script (~15s regression-managent-landmark), so the src/managent selection lands ~25-35s wall, under budget. Measured 2026-08-24 upper bounds: largest single pre-commit-tier script is regression-runner-pi-session-liveness at 20s; regression-managent-landmark 15s; the rest ≤18s. The hook prints its own elapsed on every commit ('fast tier elapsed Ns (budget 45s; 6 workers)'). New worst-case gate wall: ~25-35s (a src/managent change), under the 45s budget.

== WHAT DELETING THE RATCHET REQUIRES (D084 #3) ==
The known-red baseline is void the moment stream2b-green closes with every entry green or deleted. Deleting it requires ALL of: (1) stream2b-green resolves every `known-red` line — repair, re-point, or delete, obeying the disposition column; (2) a fresh full sweep of tools/regression-*.sh (standalone, same invocation) shows zero non-baseline failures AND zero baseline entries still failing; (3) tools/hooks/pre-commit drops the known-red read (the KNOWN_RED_FILE block in gate 3) so the gate refuses any failing script once the baseline is gone; (4) the §11 section (and its machine lines) is DELETED from spec.md, not emptied and left — an emptied-but-present baseline is a blanket ignore switch wearing a per-script mask. Expiry condition stated in spec §11: if not resolved by 2026-09-07 (two-week review), the Orchestrator must re-ratify it.

== ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE (red first, green after, narrowing, inside the hook) ==
RED FIRST: with the pre-change hook + the pre-change contract (zero declarations), a staged change to src/managent selected only the 13-script fast pool and ZERO out-of-pool managent scripts (the brief's measured consequence, reproduced). GREEN AFTER: the same staged change under the new selection selects 32 scripts, 19 of them regression-managent-* (including assert-store, attribution, holds, status-json — all outside the old pool). NARROWING: a staged change to a path no script covers (docs/README.md) selects only smoke.sh (the always-run script) and skips the coverage-declared scripts by name. Selection was exercised with a standalone harness running the hook's own selection code against synthetic staged paths (no index mutation — the live index was carrying another console's staged file at the time); the end-to-end inside-the-hook verification is this row's own commit, which the new hook validated (the hook runs the on-disk pre-commit, so committing tools/hooks/pre-commit exercises the new code).

== INSIDE-THE-HOOK VERIFICATION CAUGHT A REAL RACE (the brief's 'smoke.sh passes standalone, fails in the hook' class) ==
The first commit attempt was REFUSED by the new gate, correctly: under 6-way parallel execution, regression-claimlint-c7-json.sh (which creates a transient non-conforming fixture in findings/) raced regression-claimlint-output.sh (which requires a byte-stable live tree across two invocations) — both failed with counts that did not reproduce standalone. These were NOT in the baseline (they pass standalone), so the gate refused them as NEW failures — exactly the no-fault-of-the-author freeze the brief warned about, surfaced by the gate itself rather than discovered later. The fix (not a bypass): the regression-claimlint-* scripts now run SERIALLY before the parallel batch (spec §9.1 and the hook), removing the race while keeping the src/managent suite inside budget. This is the load-bearing evidence that the inside-the-hook verification is what found the defect, not the standalone selection harness. The 'tools/smoke.sh failed inside the hook because its output is a pipe' hazard is independently neutralized: the new gate writes each script's output to a per-script temp file (not a command-substitution pipe), so smoke.sh no longer sees a pipe on its stdout.
